To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed DNA origami nanoarrays for the multivalent investigation, with nanospatial resolution, of ligand-receptors interactions in cell spreading.

the DNA origami nanoarrays we developed permit the multivalent investigation, with nanospatial resolution, of ligand-receptors molecule interactions, with single-molecule and single-nucleotide control.
we have developed a platform for the study, at the nanoscale, of multivalent interactions in cancer cell behavior with single-molecule resolution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new nanoscale tools to study biological processes with nanoscale control and spatial resolution.
the development and application of DNA origami nanoarrays to study multivalent interactions that modulate cell spreading and cancer progression.
the design and synthesis of DNA nanostructures for the fabrication of multivalent nanoarrays for the investigation of biological processes with nanoscale control and spatial resolution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study presents a strategy for the design of biomimetic DNA nanostructures that permits the multivallent investigation of ligand–receptor molecule interactions in cell spreading with nanoscale control and spatial resolution.
we have developed a platform that allows for the investigation of the multivalent interactions of cancer cell receptors with ligands with nanoscale precision and single-molecule resolution.
this work represents a significant advance in the development of nanobiotechnologies for the investigation of biological processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we developed a platform to control the spatial organization of multivalent ligand binding sites with nanometer precision and demonstrated its application in studying the cooperative effect of integrin and epidermal-growth-factor binding in the spreading of cutaneous melanoma cancer cells.
we have demonstrated that DNA origami nanoarrays can be used as an enabling tool to study multivalent interactions with nanoscale control and single-molecule sensitivity.
we developed a DNA origami-based platform to control the nanometer-scale organization of multivalent ligands that modulated the spreading of human epidermal cancer cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we can control the nanospatial arrangement of multivalent biomolecular ligands to study the cooperative behavior of cell-surface receptor molecules with nanoscale resolution and single-molecular control.
the DNA origami technology is a powerful tool to fabricate nanoscale biomimetic structures with multivalent ligands that can be used in cell biology studies.

DNA origami can be used to control nanoscale spatial arrangement of multivalent ligand molecules on a surface, which can be used to study the effect of multivalent interactions in biological processes.
